answer: Each epoch the verifier issues a karst probe that forces the agent to pin 64 GB of RAM and answer latency checks across random offsets inside a 2 ms budget, proving physical memory instead of rented compute. A thread reply arriving late or served from swapped pages fails at once and the $500 bond is slashed. One honest agent passes on a single 64 GB node costing $120 a month, while ten fakes need 640 GB across ten separate buses for $1,200 a month, and dawn audit logs expose any shared hardware. Repeat failures freeze the identity permanently.
